newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST -Australian Sports News - Dec 3.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST -Australian Sports News - Dec 3.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Victorian cricketer and Australian Team member Matthew Elliott was forced to retire hurt yesterday after colliding mid-pitch with fellow-player Mark Waugh. Elliott will be in Melbourne tomorrow preparing for knee surgery in Melbourne while his team mates prepare to win the second Test in the five-Test series. Page 18.

After 15 seasons, 101 Wallaby caps and 64 Test tries, Rugby Union's David Campese made his exit yesterday in a 28-19 win over Wales, and has started his retirement by urging Australian officials to retain coach Greg Smith until the next World Cup in 1999. Page 18.

It is unlikely that injured Test cricket player Matthew Elliott would have been included in Australia's limited overs team even if he hadn't been injured yesterday. So too, Michael Slater may not make an appearance on the list which is set to be announced today. Page 17.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australia will attempt to spin its way to the lead in the Frank Worrell Trophy Series after Australian Cricket captain Mark Taylor showed his intentions by throwing finger-spinner Mark Waugh the new ball. Page 46.

An Australian Cricket Board will be disappointed to discover the popularity of the Sydney cricket Test has suffered by its move to November after the number of fans dropped on last year. However, this may have more to do with other factors such as rescheduling out of school holidays, a dull wicket and the lacklustre performance of Brian Lara and the West Indies. Page 46.

The annual listing of the sporting world's top earners in Forbes Magazine has seen Mike Tyson in the number one place, finishing the year with US$92 million and Australian golfer Greg Norman coming in at 38, as the only Australian and one of six non-Amerians with US$7.9 million. Page 44.
THE AGE

Keeping in line with structural changes by the AFL and Soccer Australia, the Victorian Soccer Foundation last night voted to replace its board of directors with a streamlined commission comprising seven members and the powers to co-opt two more. Page C6.
Danish Atlanta Olympics badminton coach Finn Traerup-Hansen has been appointed by Badminton Australia as the coach for the lead-up to the Sydney Olympics. Page C7.

Western Australian cricket captain Tom Moody yesterday steered the team to its first Sheffield Shield point of the season with a five-wicket win over South Australia, while Tasmania was saved from defeat by Mark Ridgeway and Mark Atkinson and went on to bat New South Wales. Page C6.
THE HERALD SUN

Trainers of star pacers Sunshine Band and Nimbo Boy, Kevin Chisolm and Alison Smith, were questioned for more than eight hours over the irregular swabs returned by the horses in June. The Harness Racing Victoria stewards who were investigating the matter eclined to pass judgement on the swabs, but have impounded the horses before finalising their inquiries. Page 63.

Olympian Clinton Robinson and former ironman Trevor Hendy, who were part of the Uncle Toby's team, have been told by company representatives that they will not be defending their kayaking title in the Murray River Marathon. Page 64.

There was a controversial dismissal yesterday at Manuka Oval in Canberra in the four-day cricket match between the ACT and England A as ACT captain-coach Mike Valetta was reported for dissent and denigrating an umpire, who called him out after first slip Craig White slicked up a low chance which was taken by wicket-keeper Warren Hegg. Page 66.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Basketball team South East Melbourne Magic has re-signed centre John Dorge for the next three years and if they are able to sign-up MVP Mike Kelly, who has stayed on in the US after the end-of-season trip, they will have their complete NBL title side. Pag 53.

Baseball player and New York Yankee major league second-baseman Pat Kelly is to play in Venezuela, ending his stint with the Adelaide Giants. The weekend-only playing schedule is said to have played a major role in the Yankee's decision to transfer Kelly.Page 53.

Dumped from the New South Wales amateur team this year, Ian Bradley raced home with a second round four-under 66 to win the New South Wales Champion of Club Champions golf tournament at Long Reef on Sunday. Page 52.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
